items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are clear (mergeConsistentHash, deduplicateHeaders, cloneConsistentHash) and doc comments are present. But the code has comments that copy the task spec, like "// Requirement 2: When disable is true..." and "// Requirement 7: ...", which don't belong in production code.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The dedup helpers are shared by build and merge, and mergeConsistentHash is registered in mergeFuncs. But mergeConsistentHash is about 70 lines with the strategy check (OverridableDeepMerge || OverridableShallowMerge) repeated, and there are four near-identical deduplicateX helpers. sourceIP cloning is also hand-copied twice.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: A Validate() hook is added and the CEL rule plus MinLength markers check input at the boundary. Merge clones slices so source IR isn't aliased. However, Terminal is *bool everywhere, and in the non-overridable disable path the code nils fields in place on p1 without recording origins. TTL parse error handling isn't visible in the diff.

items.name: Multi-policy merge semantics
items.evidence: mergeConsistentHash is registered in MergeTrafficPolicies. It unions arrays with the higher-priority entries first via deduplicateX(append(clone(higher), lower...)). The per-type arrays in the IR keep canonical order. sourceIP comes only from higher, disable is handled, and mergeOrigins.Append/SetOne records "consistentHash". Hidden tests pass.

items.name: Empty spec and disable handling
items.name_zh: 空配置与 disable 处理
items.evidence: The CEL rule "!has(self.disable) || !self.disable || (!has(self.headers) && ...)" is on the ConsistentHash type and was generated into the CRD, and Go Validate also checks it. The hasConsistentHash flag gives the default sourceIp policy for {}. Disable suppresses inherited policies in merge, and the tests cover it.
